rationale: The hypothesis posits a strict dichotomy: dominant RNU2-2 variants act via dominant-negative/toxic spliceosomal disruption, whereas recessive variants act solely through quantitative loss of U2-2 abundance without toxic spliceosomal disruption. While Jackson et al. (2026) support mechanistically distinct etiologies characterized by reduced U2-2 transcript stability and decreased U2-2/U2-1 ratios in biallelic disease, transcriptomic analyses by Henry et al. (2026) demonstrate that biallelic variants also cause aberrant splicing (mutually exclusive exons and alternative 3' splice-site usage) in fibroblasts. Furthermore, Leitão et al. (2026) observed overlapping phenotypes and variant-specific splicing/episignature effects, proposing a unified 'gradient-of-impact' model bridging dominant and recessive inheritance rather than two mutually exclusive pathogenic mechanisms.

evidence.text: Biallelic RNU2-2 variants significantly correlate with reduced U2-2 transcript abundance and compromised stability, altering the ratio of U2-2 to paralog U2-1 and supporting a loss-of-expression mechanism distinct from dominant RNU2-2 disorder.

source.title: Biallelic variants in RNU2-2 cause a remarkably frequent developmental and epileptic encephalopathy
source.quote: We find that candidate biallelic variants are significantly correlated with reduced U2-2 abundance, implicating compromised transcript stability as a probable pathomechanism. We identify a decreased ratio of U2-2 to its paralog U2-1 as a potential diagnostic biomarker for this condition. We show that the recessive RNU2-2 syndrome is genetically, clinically and mechanistically distinct from the dominant RNU2-2 disorder.

evidence.text: Systematic assessment of 141 individuals with RNU2-2 variants demonstrated overlapping clinical features between dominant and recessive forms, with blood transcriptomics and DNA methylation analyses pointing to a gradient-of-impact model bridging dominant and recessive inheritance rather than distinct segregated mechanisms.

source.title: Systematic analysis of snRNA genes reveals frequent RNU2-2 variants in dominant and recessive developmental and epileptic encephalopathies
source.quote: Dominant and recessive RNU2-2 NDDs share overlapping clinical features, with frequent epilepsy. Blood transcriptomics and DNA methylation analyses revealed subtle, variant-specific effects on splicing and episignatures. Our results support a gradient-of-impact model bridging dominant and recessive inheritance

evidence.text: Biallelic RNU2-2 variants do cause aberrant splicing in patient tissues: RNA sequencing in patient fibroblasts revealed significant aberrant splicing events, specifically mutually exclusive exon usage and alternative 3' splice-site selection, refuting the notion that recessive mutations lack spliceosomal disruption.

source.title: Phenotypic and transcriptomic characterization of biallelic RNU2‐2 developmental and epileptic encephalopathy
source.quote: RNA sequencing analyses showed aberrant splicing, with the most pronounced effects in fibroblast tissues in mutually exclusive exon and alternate 3' splice-site events, which were not detectable in blood.

evidence.text: RNA sequencing in patient fibroblasts with de novo dominant RNU2-2 variants showed no distinct transcriptomic signature in one tested patient, challenging the view of robust detectable toxic splicing disruption in dominant cases.

source.title: Prominent Movement Disorders in RNU2‐2‐Related Spliceosomopathy
source.journal: Annals of Clinical and Translational Neurology
source.quote: RNA sequencing of fibroblasts in one patient showed no characteristic transcriptomic signature. Spliceosomopathies should be considered in neurodevelopmental disorders and developmental and epileptic encephalopathies with hyperkinetic features.

numbers.metric: patients identified with recurrent de novo RNU2-2 variants

conflicts: Jackson et al. (2026) report that recessive RNU2-2 syndrome is mechanistically distinct from dominant disorder due to reduced transcript stability/abundance, whereas Henry et al. (2026) demonstrate that biallelic variants directly lead to spliceosomal dysfunction with missplicing (alternate 3' splice sites and mutually exclusive exons) in patient fibroblasts.

Leitão et al. (2026) propose a gradient-of-impact model linking dominant and recessive variants with overlapping phenotypes and variant-specific splicing and episignature impacts, contradicting a clean binary dichotomy of dominant-negative toxicity versus purely quantitative transcript loss.

new_directions.question_text: Does tissue-specific expression of RNU2-2 and its paralog RNU2-1 modulate spliceosomal misprocessing in neural versus non-neural cell types?
new_directions.rationale: Blood transcriptomics failed to detect the missplicing readily evident in fibroblasts in Henry et al. (2026); resolving tissue-specific U2-2:U2-1 stoichiometry in neuronal lineages will clarify whether quantitative depletion leads directly to downstream spliceosomal errors.

new_directions.question_text: Do dominant and recessive RNU2-2 variants induce convergent or distinct genome-wide DNA episignatures?
new_directions.rationale: Leitão et al. noted variant-specific episignatures; comparing episignature patterns across large cohorts of dominant vs biallelic cases can objectively quantify whether epigenetic dysregulation reflects a shared gradient or mutually exclusive mechanistic pathways.
